subject: Monthly metrics flash — sprintboard & QBR prep
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Monthly metrics flash — sprintboard & QBR prep

Team — attaching the month-end snapshot (CSV) and a short note on the signals I want on the QBR readout. Summary first:

- Latency: P95 increased from 120ms -> 185ms on 5/12 during a usage burst. Root cause looks like a kernel fallback on the cuda path for one model variant.
- Cost: token unit cost improved by 6% month-over-month thanks to wider batching, but caching hit-rate dropped 4% (prefix churn).
- Uptime: Platform SLO at 99.95% still met, but two customer-facing brief incidents (5/12 and 5/16) added noise for execs.
- Usage: 28% MoM growth in inference calls; top growth from a single partner (QuantumCloud POC).

Action asks for prep:
1) Tessa — can you validate the P95 regression graph and add the per-model breakdown as a slide? I put a placeholder in the QBR draft.
2) Markus — confirm cost delta origin (batching vs quantization) and whether we need a rollback for the new kernel.
3) Irene — any leadership spin / ask we should prep for (credits, escalation notes) ahead of the QBR on 6/2?

Attached: 2026-05-monthly-dashboard.csv, qbr-draft-v1.pptx (draft slide 3 is the metrics), latency-regression-snapshot.png

Thanks — will stitch into the QBR deck once we have updates.

Connor O'Brien
Lead, Inference Platform
Redwood Inference

Thanks Connor — quick updates from my side after a first pass on the CSV and the snapshot:

- I reproduced the P95 spike in the infra data (edge region us-west-2) and isolated it to model 'redwood-lambda-7B-quant' under long-context workloads (>1024 tokens).
- I prepared a per-model chart (slide 3.2) showing baseline vs spike; will add code snippets for how we traced KV cache pressure.
- For the QBR, propose we present a single remediation plan slide (short-term config rollback + longer-term kernel tune).

Open question: do we want to ask for an exception to the change window to push a targeted kernel fix? If leadership wants a hard SLA on P95 we should propose a timeline.

Att: added notes to qbr-draft-v1.pptx (commented slide 3.2)

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Monthly metrics flash — sprintboard & QBR prep

Connor / team — thanks for the clear note. A few leadership items to align before the QBR: 

- Communication: we should lead with the customer impact narrative (two short incidents) and our mitigation plan. Avoid deep infra detail in the first slides; give a one-slide technical appendix for reviewers.
- Credits ask: customer-outreach suggests Acme may ask for a one-off credit for the 5/12 incident. I am OK with an offer conditioned on a remediation timeline and a post-mortem.
- Exec ask: request 3 weeks for a targeted kernel hotfix and a 6-week window for full validation and rollout. If we need faster runway we may ask for temporary burst capacity credits (finance sign-off).

Please add a short 'customer impact' slide and a proposed timeline (Irene-approved) to the deck. Also, Connor — loop in Sales for Acme dialog; I want to see the outreach note before it goes out.

Irene Choi
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
